summary: The NNPC/SNEPCo National University Scholarship is Shell Nigeria's deep-water joint venture award for Nigerian students in their second year at a public university. It pays a yearly grant (N250,000 in the 2025 call) from 200 level until graduation, as long as you keep a CGPA of 3.5. Winners are strong students who pass a proctored computer-based test; the top 10 in each state and the FCT go forward.
lookfor: A first-year CGPA of at least 3.5 on a 5-point scale (or equivalent)
Your score in the proctored computer-based test (CBT) - this decides the ranking
Ranking within your state of origin: top 10 per state plus FCT go to verification
Genuine documents that pass academic verification (falsified results mean disqualification)
Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply
cycle: The 2025 call opened in July 2025 and closed on 29 August 2025 (CBT and verification followed). A 2026 call was not confirmed when checked on 7 Oct 2026; past rounds have opened between June and August, so prepare from your 100-level year and watch from June 2027.

eligibility.no: This award is for Nigerians only. Look at awards open to your nationality in Laureate Lab.

eligibility.q: Are you in your second year (200 level) of a full-time first degree at an NUC-accredited public (federal or state) university?
eligibility.no: If you are in 100 level, prepare now and apply next year. If you are past 200 level, try the NNPC/Seplat JV award (200 level and above) or MTN STS (300 level).

eligibility.q: Is your first-year CGPA 3.5 or higher on a 5-point scale (or equivalent)?
eligibility.no: You cannot apply this round. Try awards with lower cut-offs, and work on your grades: scholars must keep 3.5 every session anyway.

eligibility.q: Are you free of any other scholarship from an oil and gas company or a national/international body?
eligibility.no: You must choose. Holding two oil and gas awards breaks the rules and can lead to withdrawal.

eligibility.q: Can you get a letter from your Local Government Area confirming your state of origin?
eligibility.no: Visit your LGA secretariat early. Without it the state quota cannot be applied to you.

eligibility.q: Are you an indigene of Bayelsa, Delta, Imo or Rivers State?
eligibility.no: Not required for SNEPCo. If yes, also look at the NNPC-Renaissance JV award, which has an extra 'areas of operation' quota for those states.

steps.title: Check you fit the rules and know which Shell-linked award this is
steps.why: Many students mix up the SNEPCo award with the old Shell SPDC JV award, which since 2025 runs as the NNPC-Renaissance JV award with different dates and portal.
do: Read the eligibility questions above and answer each honestly.
Open the 2025 SNEPCo scheme page on Scholastica and read last year's rules so you know what to expect.
Write down your level, your university type (federal or state) and your first-year CGPA.
Open the Renaissance education page. If you are an indigene of Bayelsa, Delta, Imo or Rivers, plan to apply to that award too.
Note: you may not hold two oil and gas scholarships at the same time. If you win both, you must pick one.
tips: Selection is mostly the test score plus state ranking. Your CGPA gets you in; the CBT decides who wins.
Shell Nigeria's own pages are on shell.com.ng. SNEPCo applications have run on candidate.scholastica.ng. Anything else is a copy.
avoid: Assuming private universities qualify - the call says public, NUC-accredited universities.
Waiting until the call opens to check your CGPA. Ask your department for your first-year result early.
check: I am in 200 level at a public university.
My first-year CGPA is 3.5 or more.
I know SNEPCo and NNPC-Renaissance are separate calls.

steps.title: Learn how to spot a fake announcement
steps.why: Every year fake 'Shell scholarship' pages ask students to pay or share bank details. One mistake can cost you money and your data.
do: Bookmark shell.com.ng and candidate.scholastica.ng. Only trust a call you can reach from one of these.
If you see the call on a blog or WhatsApp, open the official site yourself (type the address) and confirm it is there.
Check the announcement says the application is free. Shell-linked JV awards do not charge fees.
Never send your BVN, ATM PIN, bank login or a 'processing fee' to anyone.
Ask your university's Students Affairs or scholarship office if the call is real - they usually receive the official notice.
tips: The application is free. Anyone asking you to pay for a form, 'processing', a test slot or 'guaranteed selection' is a scammer.
Never use an 'agent' or cybercafe operator to apply for you with their email. Use your own email and phone so the funder's messages reach you.
avoid: Clicking shortened links (bit.ly etc.) shared in groups without checking where they lead.
Trusting a WhatsApp number that 'helps with the test' for a fee.
check: I know the two official places to check.
I will never pay to apply.

steps.title: Build your timeline from June to the results
steps.why: The window is short (about four to six weeks). Students who prepare documents before it opens submit calmly and early.
do: Open a calendar and mark 1 June as 'start checking for the SNEPCo call'.
Mark the likely closing period (late July to end of August, based on 2025).
Book time each week from June for CBT practice (see the test step).
Set reminders to check your email (including spam) daily after you submit - shortlisting and test invitations come by email/SMS.
Add the NNPC-Renaissance and NNPC/Seplat calls to the same calendar so you do not miss them.
tips: Treat 'due' days in this guide as days before the closing date.
Keep all documents in one Google Drive or phone folder named 'SNEPCo'.
avoid: Planning to start on the last week - portals slow down near deadlines.
check: I have a dated plan and reminders set.

steps.title: Create your Scholastica account with your own email
steps.why: Your account is where you submit, receive updates and possibly test details. A wrong email means you miss the invitation.
do: When the call is live, open the SNEPCo scheme link from Shell or Scholastica (in 2025 it was candidate.scholastica.ng/schemes/NNPCLTDSNEPCo25).
Register with a personal email you check daily (Gmail or similar), your real name as on your documents, and your own phone number.
Write your login details in a safe place (not in a group chat).
Fill your personal details once and check spelling of your name against your JAMB letter.
tips: Use the same spelling of your name on every document; differences cause verification problems.
avoid: Using a cybercafe operator's email or phone number.
Creating two accounts - duplicate applications can be disqualified.
check: I can log in and see the scheme.
My email and phone are mine.

steps.title: Get your first-year result showing your CGPA
steps.why: The call asks for an academic transcript showing your 100-level CGPA (two completed semesters). Without it you are not eligible.
do: Go to your department or faculty office and ask for a signed and stamped statement of result or student copy of your 100-level results showing the CGPA.
If your school has a student portal, print or download the result page as well.
Scan it clearly as PDF or JPG. Check every number is readable.
If your CGPA is on a 4- or 7-point scale, keep a note of your school's grading scale to show it is equivalent to 3.5/5.
tips: Start this the moment you finish 100-level exams - signatures can take weeks.
avoid: Uploading a blurred phone photo.
Rounding up your CGPA - verification will catch it.
check: I have a clear, stamped copy showing my CGPA.

steps.title: Collect admission, JAMB and O-level documents
steps.why: These prove you are a genuine student and are checked at verification.
do: Print or download your JAMB admission letter from the JAMB portal and your university admission letter.
Get your UTME result slip.
Find your O-level results (WAEC/NECO/NABTEB) and any A-level/OND/NCE results if you have them. Print the online result with the scratch-card checker if you lack the certificate.
Scan each as a separate clear file and name it (e.g. 'JAMB_admission_letter.pdf').
tips: Keep originals safe; you may need to show them at verification.
avoid: Mixing up the JAMB admission letter and the university admission letter - upload both if asked.
check: I have admission letters, UTME result and O-level result scanned.

links.t: 2025 NNPC-SNEPCo scheme page on Scholastica (closed; shows last year's rules)

steps.title: Get your Local Government identification letter
steps.why: The award uses state quotas, so you must prove your state and LGA of origin with an official letter.
do: Go to your LGA secretariat (or the office your state uses) and ask for a certificate or letter of identification showing your LGA of origin.
Take your passport photo, a parent's ID or your NIN slip; many LGAs ask for these.
Pay only the official fee and collect a receipt.
Scan the letter clearly.
tips: If you live far from your LGA, ask a parent to request it in person on your behalf early.
avoid: Using a letter from your state of residence instead of your state of origin.
check: I have an LGA letter that names my LGA and state of origin.

links.t: 2025 NNPC-SNEPCo scheme page on Scholastica (closed; shows last year's rules)

steps.title: Prepare your photo and the declaration form
steps.why: The 2025 call required a passport photo (JPEG, max 200KB) and a completed government official declaration form. Wrong file sizes stop uploads.
do: Take a recent passport photo on a white background. Save as JPEG and reduce it to under 200KB (any free image compressor works).
Download the declaration form from the scheme page when the call opens.
Fill it, get it signed by the official named on the form, sign it yourself, and scan it.
Check the current guidance for any new document added this year.
tips: Allow time for the official's signature - they may be away.
avoid: Uploading a selfie or a photo with a busy background.
check: My photo is JPEG and under 200KB.
My declaration form is signed and scanned.

steps.title: Practise for the computer-based test
steps.why: Only eligible candidates are invited to the proctored CBT, and the top 10 per state go forward. The test is where you win or lose.
do: Expect aptitude-style questions: verbal reasoning, numerical reasoning (percentages, ratios, data tables) and logical reasoning. Check the invitation for the exact format.
Practise timed sets daily. Aim for speed and accuracy, not just correct answers.
Practise on a computer, not only on paper, so the screen format feels normal.
If the test is remotely proctored, test your laptop camera, microphone and internet in advance and choose a quiet, well-lit room.
tips: Review every wrong answer and write why it was wrong.
Sleep well the night before; arrive or log in early.
avoid: Paying anyone who claims to sell 'leaked questions' - this is a scam and cheating leads to disqualification.
check: I can finish a 30-question timed set calmly.
My device and internet work for an online test.

steps.title: Fill the form and upload documents
steps.why: A complete, accurate form is your ticket to the test. Mistakes here are the most common reason for being dropped.
do: Log in to Scholastica and open the SNEPCo scheme.
Fill personal details, state and LGA of origin, university, course, level and CGPA exactly as on your documents.
Upload each document in the right slot. Open each upload preview to check it is the correct file.
Read the whole form again before you press submit.
tips: Submit at least a week before the deadline; portals slow down in the last days.
avoid: Typing your state of residence where it asks for state of origin.
Leaving optional-looking fields that are actually needed.
check: Every field matches my documents.
All uploads open and are readable.

steps.title: Submit, save proof and watch your inbox
steps.why: Proof of submission protects you if there is a dispute, and invitations to the test come by email or SMS.
do: Press submit and wait for the confirmation screen or email.
Screenshot or save the confirmation as PDF.
Add the Scholastica sender to your contacts so messages do not go to spam.
Check email (and spam) daily until the test date is announced.
tips: Tell a parent or friend the expected test period so you can plan travel if a centre is used.
avoid: Assuming silence means rejection - check the portal itself too.
check: I have saved proof of submission.

links.t: 2025 NNPC-SNEPCo scheme page on Scholastica (closed; shows last year's rules)

steps.title: Take the proctored CBT
steps.why: Your test score decides your rank in your state.
do: Read the invitation carefully: date, time, whether it is at a centre or online, and what ID to bring.
Bring or have ready your ID (school ID, NIN slip or other valid ID) and the invitation.
Start early. Follow every proctoring rule (no phones, no other people in the room for online tests).
Manage time: skip hard questions and return to them.
tips: If online, close all other apps and keep your charger plugged in.
avoid: Logging in late or from a noisy place.
Using any outside help - proctoring flags it.
check: I know where/how and when my test is.

steps.title: Pass verification and accept the award
steps.why: The top 10 per state and FCT go to academic verification before any offer. Falsified results lead to disqualification.
do: If contacted, take your original documents to the verification as instructed (or upload as asked).
Make sure your university can confirm your CGPA if they are contacted.
Read the award letter. Note the renewal rule: keep a CGPA of at least 3.5 every session.
Give your bank details only through the official channel named in the award letter, never to a caller.
tips: Keep copies of every letter; you will need them each year for renewal.
avoid: Missing the verification date because you changed phone number.
check: I understand I must keep 3.5 CGPA each year.

steps.title: If you were not selected, prepare for other awards
steps.why: You can usually only apply once (in 200 level), so redirect your effort quickly.
do: Check the NNPC/Seplat JV award (200 level and above; opens around Feb-Mar).
Check MTN STS when you reach 300 level (opens around Apr-May).
If you are from Bayelsa, Delta, Imo or Rivers, check the NNPC-Renaissance JV award.
Keep your documents folder up to date - most Nigerian corporate awards ask for the same items.
tips: Your CBT practice transfers directly to other oil and gas scholarship tests.
avoid: Giving up on scholarships after one try.
check: I have my next award on the calendar.

faq.a: The 2025 call was reported as N250,000 a year, from 200 level to graduation, if you keep a 3.5 CGPA. Check the current call for the amount.

faq.q: Is it the same as the Shell SPDC JV scholarship?
faq.a: No. Shell sold its onshore SPDC business; that award now runs as the NNPC-Renaissance JV University Scholarship. SNEPCo is Shell's deep-water joint venture and has its own call.
The 2025 call was for public (federal or state) NUC-accredited universities only.

faq.q: I am in 300 level. Can I apply?
faq.a: No, the call is for students in their second year. Look at NNPC/Seplat JV or MTN STS.

faq.q: How do I know a call is real?
faq.a: Find it yourself on shell.com.ng or candidate.scholastica.ng, confirm it is free, and ask your university scholarship office. Ignore posts asking for fees or bank details.

faq.q: Does it come with an internship or job?
faq.a: Not as part of the grant. Treat it as a yearly cash award.
